policy_title: Reform House of Lords and Strengthen Democracy
stated: Labour will immediately modernise the House of Lords by legislating to remove the right of hereditary peers to sit and vote, introducing a mandatory retirement age of 80, strengthening rules for removing disgraced members, and reforming the appointments process. The party is committed to replacing the House of Lords with an alternative, more representative second chamber, consulting the public on proposals. They will also improve voter registration, address voter ID inconsistencies (e.g., for veteran cards), give 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote in all elections, and strengthen rules on political party donations.

source.quote: The next Labour government will therefore bring about an immediate modernisation, by introducing legislation to remove the right of hereditary peers to sit and vote in the House of Lords. Labour will also introduce a mandatory retirement age. At the end of the Parliament in which a member reaches 80 years of age, they will be required to retire from the House of Lords. Labour will ensure all peers meet the high standards the public expect of them, and we will introduce a new participation requirement as well as strengthening the circumstances in which disgraced members can be removed. We will reform the appointments process to ensure the quality of new appointments and will seek to improve the national and regional balance of the second chamber. Whilst this action to modernise the House of Lords will be an improvement, Labour is committed to replacing the House of Lords with an alternative second chamber that is more representative of the regions and nations. Labour will consult on proposals, seeking the input of the British public on how politics can best serve them. To encourage participation in our democracy, Labour will improve voter registration and address the inconsistencies in voter ID rules that prevent legitimate voters from voting. For example, in the case of HM Armed Forces Veteran Cards. We will increase participation the engagement of young people in our vibrant democracy, by giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote in all elections. And we will protect democracy by strengthening the rules around donations to political parties.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly alters democratic and voting rights (extending the franchise to 16–17-year-olds, improving voter registration, addressing voter ID rules), the composition and accountability of a legislative chamber, and the rules governing political donations — all squarely within O9's 'voting & democratic rights' and 'due process' indicators.

membership_note: The policy is squarely a package of democratic and constitutional reforms. Effects on other fundamentals (e.g. O15 via civic participation, O12 via any implementation cost) are too indirect or negligible to clear the non-negligible bar independently; O9 is the sole material bearing.
